title: Launching a paid media campaign
instructions: Put the seven stages of a Brightline Media campaign launch in the order they happen. Drag the rows or use the arrow buttons.

items.text: Receive and clarify the client brief
items.description: Everything downstream depends on the objective, budget, audience and timing agreed here.

items.text: Research the audience and the competition
items.description: Audience insights and competitor spend shape the channel mix before any money is committed.

items.text: Build the media plan and budget split
items.description: Channels, flighting and the budget split are proposed only once the research is in.
Creative is cut to the formats the plan requires, so it follows the plan, not the other way round.

items.text: Set up campaigns, tracking and QA
items.description: Ads, audiences and conversion tracking are configured and checked before anything goes live.
Once live, bids, budgets and creative rotation are tuned against the plan's targets.

items.text: Report results and recommend next steps
items.description: The wrap-up report closes the loop and feeds the next brief.

content.explanation: The sequence runs from understanding (brief, research) to planning, to production (creative, setup), and finally to execution and learning (launch, report). Skipping a step usually means redoing a later one.
content.hint: You cannot plan what you have not researched, and you cannot build what you have not planned.

feedback.complete: That is the Brightline launch playbook. Keep it handy for your first campaign.
